question: Compare what the Matrice 210 V1 and the Autel EVO Max 4N do with altitude when RTH starts near the Home Point.

intake.decided_by: code (single pass has no intake call)

brief.short_answer: Gaps exist in explicit altitude behavior for Autel near Home Point and in cross-reference between manufacturer guidance and FAA risk guidance. The DJI Matrice 210 V1 specifies adjustable RTH altitude with a rule that it will elevate to a Failsafe Altitude and descend/land within a 65 ft radius of Home Point, but Autel EVO Max 4N does not state a similar altitude rule during RTH. Incident reports show Autel’s RTH can fail or be unresponsive, highlighting real-world variability. Overall, DJI provides a clear altitude framework for RTH near Home Point, while Autel’s guidance defers altitude decisions to signals and user-selected actions, creating ambiguity without further detail.

claims.text: Autel EVO Max 4N Signal Lost behavior includes Return to Home, Hover, and Land; Signal Loss Action options include Continue mission and Auto RTH; reconnection attempts occur, with action taken if reconnection fails.
claims.quote: The drone's Signal Lost behavior options include Return to Home, Hover, and Land. Signal Loss Action options include Continue mission and Auto RTH. When the C2 link is lost, the Autel Enterprise App will issue real-time voice alerts to notify the user.

claims.text: Autel EVO Max 4N does not specify an altitude-change rule near the Home Point during RTH; guidance centers on reconnection attempts and selected Signal Loss behavior.
claims.quote: During the execution of automatic RTH caused by signal loss, the drone will continue to attempt to reconnect. If reconnection is not established within 10 seconds, the Autel Enterprise App will display the warning... and the drone will execute the preset Signal Loss Action or Signal Lost behavior accordingly.

claims.text: DJI Matrice 210 V1 uses an adjustable RTH altitude and elevates to a Failsafe Altitude when RTH is triggered near the Home Point.
claims.quote: RTH (Adjustable Altitude) Height over HP<=Failsafe Altitude Height over HP>Failsafe Altitude Elevate to Failsafe Altitude

claims.text: DJI Matrice 210 V1 will descend and land if RTH is triggered within 65 feet (20 m) of the Home Point and GPS is sufficient; it cannot return when GPS is weak/unavailable.
claims.quote: The aircraft will automatically descend and land if RTH is triggered when the aircraft flies within a 65 feet (20 meters) radius of the Home Point.

claims.text: Incident report indicates Autel EVO Max 4N lost control shortly after takeoff with Return To Home failing and the platform unrecovered.
claims.quote: Shortly after takeoff I completely lost control of the UAS. Platform continued to fly away from me while input into the controls to return. All attempts of Return To Home features failed. UAS Platform has not been located or recovered.

gaps.text: No explicit Autel altitude behavior near Home Point during RTH stated in manuals.
FAA guidance passages do not directly specify altitude behavior for RTH near Home Point for these models.
Exact operational criteria when RTH starts near Home Point for Autel (e.g., whether altitude is adjusted) is unclear from the sources.
Autel claims of RTH behavior rely on signal-loss actions; DJI provides a defined Failsafe Altitude behavior—potentially conflicting operational expectations in a shared airspace context.
Cross-model comparatives may be incomplete without FAA guidance tying to model-specific RTH altitude rules.
No verification of whether Autel’s 10-second reconnection window applies identically across environments near Home Point.
